# Research across all Monitoring agencies jurisdictions — 25 September 2026

## Scope and limits

Roster: all 36 jurisdictions in monitoring-agencies-information.md at main commit 7357b8692f6c1f0cd3415c3f714765627e74b7dd. Research began 11:49 UTC; external discovery ended before 12:19 UTC, within the 30-minute pass. No country received more than ten minutes of active research. Failed document/detail URLs were not pursued indefinitely. Subsequent work is presentation, validation and review, not renewed research.

This is an initial bounded public-source investigation for every jurisdiction, not an exhaustive sector-by-sector audit. Each JSON records actual search terms, checked or attempted sources, findings, limitations and follow-up. A no-findings result applies only to its stated sources. Incomplete or blocked investigations remain partially_researched. Existing claims and prior investigations remain in their records.

Eight new records: Canada, Faroe Islands, Greenland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, United Kingdom and Åland. Åland uses the EU territory classification introduced separately in PR #58. The other 28 records are updated. No placeholders added to the public page.

## Publication changes and evidence

Seven new primary-source findings: Finland consumer-service complaints/enquiries; France interim e-commerce checks; Germany MLBF monitoring; Ireland EAA submissions; Slovenia tested audiovisual features; Canada federal accessibility-document inspections; UK public-sector monitoring and voluntary compliance. Canada and UK remain explicitly other-law examples in the non-EU section. The UK source is historical (2022–2024), not presented as a current snapshot.

Public rows: three existing rows extended (Finland, France agency, Ireland) and four added (Germany agency, Slovenia audiovisual, Canada, United Kingdom). Exact new paragraphs match the isolated reviewers’ proposed-text file SHA256 e4b6f083a24b30e53db31213f440cd6da421fde3caf7a2982891fb8c9616a057. Source labels and links were added for each paragraph. Date added values retained; updated dates describe these edits.

Retained legacy claims are NOT newly verified: Finland’s four September statistics lines; Ireland’s Deque-attributed ComReg/Three claim. Their wording is unchanged and their unknown/secondary evidence statuses remain in JSON. France’s pre-existing agency claims retain prior verified claim references and the previous audit reports. Other unchanged public rows, including Austria, Denmark, Germany’s overlay claim, Slovenia’s unlinked warning/no-fines statement, Sweden’s correspondence statistics, France’s litigation and the Commission/Norway entries, are not re-certified by this review. The frozen baseline is unchanged.

PRs #56–58 are merged into the current base. Estonia’s independently reviewed correspondence claims and public row are preserved from PR #57; the earlier derivative lead is superseded. Belgium and Luxembourg retain the cross-page leads and remain partially researched. France’s corrected declaration link is preserved. This reconciliation adds no new external research or public wording.

## Access and document review

- Ireland: annual report downloaded (about 5.8 MB); PDF page 11 rendered and visually read, including the column break between EAA context and figures.
- Hungary: five-page inspection programme downloaded (about 145 KB); text examined. Generic online-sales/vulnerable-consumer headings do not establish EAA activity.
- France: official press index and three-page PDF text retrieved. Direct PDF download returned 403; web screenshot did not produce an image visible to the reviewer. The interim numbers are in a plain paragraph on page 2, not a visual-only chart. No visual PDF check claimed.
- Latvia: report text retrieved through web; download failed HTTP/2. No assertion of exhaustive absence based on PDF text search.
- Malta and Romania: annual-report retrieval/download failed, including 403 responses. No factual outcomes inferred from snippets.
- Slovenia: two e-book decision detail links failed twice; index references remain leads only. RTV decision summary was retrieved.
- No browser security denials were bypassed. No emails or forms submitted. No large binary source files committed.

## Isolated reviews

Source fidelity: /root/wide_fidelity, fork_turns=none, received original passages, URLs/sections and exact proposed text only. Final verdict Supported for all seven entries. Removed the explanatory Germany EAA clause that was not established in the supplied passage; retained computer-only testing condition for Slovenia; distinguished planned French action and Irish submissions from decisions. Final text hash above.

Readability: /root/wide_readability, fork_turns=none, received proposed public text only. Final Pass for all seven entries, broadly B2. Optional stylistic changes were not applied after the final pass; no new facts were introduced.

Independent PR review: /root/wide_pr_final, fork_turns=none, reviewed actual PR #59 at d4a143826a0bc1dc79dcd06adde5128f685cb969 against main f7c09033ca21146d46d4fffae6d162e748f08723. No substantive findings. Independently reran the checker, all 26 tests and verification-date check. Reviewed the actual diff, claim preservation, evidence mappings, row fingerprints, routing and description. No renewed source retrieval or retranslations; source assessment used recorded passages and completed isolated-review reports. This is not maintainer approval. Subsequent changes only record this verdict and PR references; public wording and evidence are unchanged.

## Local validation

Enforcement checker: PASS, 36 records and 18 mapped public rows. Regression suite: 26 tests pass, including the separate territory prerequisite. Markdownlint: zero issues. Verification-date script: no last_verified markers. These checks do not verify legal meaning or live links. Source access is described above; no blanket link-check pass is claimed. Local rendering produced the same five warnings from the installed legacy HTML Tidy as current main (document wrapper and table summary attributes); no clean HTML-validation pass is claimed. GitHub had registered no workflow runs or check runs for the reviewed head at delivery, so CI is unconfirmed.

## Manual checks before merge

Prerequisite PRs #56–58 have merged; the research PR targets current main. No additional factual publication blocker identified after narrowing the additions. Ordinary maintainer review remains required.

## Nonblocking follow-up

Continue jurisdiction-specific gaps recorded in JSON. Priorities include Estonia subsequent outcomes, Slovenia e-book decisions, inaccessible annual reports, unresolved inherited statistics and broader sector/court coverage. France’s final investigation results are expected in early 2027; that is a source expectation, not a scheduled monitor. No automation created.
